title: Jesse Price, the cat-o'-nine-tails and whipping Billie
summary: Simmons bought a whip with Jesse Price and used it on Billie.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: So one day, God Bless the Dead, Jesse Price came to New York. First person he come to see was Lady Day. That's where I met Jesse Price. So I was leaving out and I say man, come on and go with me. I went outside and got the bus down to 50th and Broadway. No, we didn't get the bus, we got the subway, I'm sorry. And come up on the 8th Avenue side of 50th street. And there was a pet shop across the street and went over and bought a cat of nine tails. Jesse Price was falling over car hoods in hysterics. So the man at the pet shop says, the state only gives us three tails. I say well I have a great dane that is very unruly, I say give me the three. So I say what time will he be ready. He told me. So Jesse, still in stitches. We went to the theatre on 42nd Street to catch a movie and every now and then at the movie, Jesse would think about it and put his hand on his head and just crack up laughing. He'd say man

you're something else. So no sooner we get back home before we could get to work, she had to go into her act. And I showed her this whip when I walked in, just like you show a dog or a cat, you know where he had piddled on the floor, you know, I showed her this whip and I hung it on the door knob. I'm tired of using my hands. And I caught her with this whip. She wanted to jump out the fourth floor. I hit her every where but in her face and the bottom of her feet.

And Monty Kaye, who's executive producer for Flip Wilson, he was running around, running errands for Billy and waking her up for interviews and for different things so he got an apartment next door --
